2 Diksha 15

3 : 2

x = 880

questions.question: A can complete some work in 35 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They worked together for 8 days, then B left the work. In how many days will A alone complete 60% of the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete some work in 35 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They worked together for 8 days, then B left the work. In how many days will A alone complete 60% of the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Given :

A can complete a work in = 35 days

B can complete a work in = 15 days

Formula used: Work = Efficiency× Time

Calculation :

Let :

Total work = LCM of 35,15 = 105

Efficiency of A = 105/35 = 3 unit 

Efficiency of B = 105/15 = 7 unit 

According to Question they work together for 8 days, B left then A will complete the work 

⇒ (A+B)8 +AX = 105

⇒ 10 × 8 + 3X= 105×

⇒ 80 +3X = 105

⇒ 3X = 25× 3/5      ( In Question it is mentioned that A alone complete 60% of remaining work )

⇒ X = 5 days

So, A alone complete 60% of the remaining work in 5 days.

Alternate Method

  Time Total work  Efficiency
A 35 105 3
B 15 7

 

 

 

Efficiency of  work of A and B in one days = 3 + 7

⇒ 10 

Total work done by A and B both in 8 days = 10 × 8

⇒ 80 

According to Question they work together for 8 days and B left then remaining work = 105 - 80 = 25

60% of remaining work = 25 × 60% = 15

A alone complete 60% of remaining work = 15/3 = 5

So, A alone complete 60% of the remaining work in 5 days.

questions.question: A can do a work in 4 days and B in 12 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then the fraction of the work that will be left is:
questions.questionHtml: A can do a work in 4 days and B in 12 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then the fraction of the work that will be left is:
questions.solution:
Given : 

A can do a piece of work in 4 days

B can do a piece of work in 12 days

They worked together for 2 days.

Formula Used : 

Work done = time × efficiency

Calculation : 

Total work = LCM(4,12) = 12

Efficiency of A = 3

Efficiency of B = 1

Work done in 2 days = 2 × (3 + 1) = 8

Fraction of work still left = 4/12 = 1/3

∴ The correct answer is 1/3.

questions.question: P can fill a tank in 5 hours. Q can fill the same tank in 10 hours. R can empty the same tank in 20 hours. How much time will all the three take together to fill the same tank?
questions.questionHtml: P can fill a tank in 5 hours. Q can fill the same tank in 10 hours. R can empty the same tank in 20 hours. How much time will all the three take together to fill the same tank?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total capacity (Total Work) = LCM(5, 10, 20) = 20 units.

Efficiency of P = 20 ÷ 5 = +4 units/hr

Efficiency of Q = 20 ÷ 10 = +2 units/hr

Efficiency of R = 20 ÷ 20 = −1 units/hr (negative work)

Combined efficiency = 4 + 2 − 1 = 5 units/hr

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by pipe P to fill the tank = 5 hours

Time taken by pipe Q to fill the tank = 10 hours

Time taken by pipe R to empty the tank = 20 hours

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Note: Work done by an emptying pipe is considered negative.

Pipe Hours Total Work Efficiency
P 5 20 +4
Q 10 +2
R 20 −1

Calculations:

⇒ Total Efficiency of P, Q, and R working together = (+4) + (+2) + (−1)

⇒ Total Efficiency = 6 − 1 = 5 units/hour

⇒ Total time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Total time taken = 20 ÷ 5

⇒ Total time taken = 4 hours

∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.

Additional Information

Pipes & Cisterns vs Time & Work

The underlying concept is exactly identical to standard Time & Work. The only difference is that an outlet pipe or a leak is assigned negative efficiency.

Combined Efficiency Rule

If two pipes A and B can fill a tank in x and y hours, and pipe C empties it in z hours, their combined 1-hour work = (1/x) + (1/y) − (1/z).

Tank Capacity Formula

If the absolute flow rate (liters/min or liters/hour) of any pipe is known, then Tank Capacity = Total filling/emptying time of that pipe × Flow rate.

questions.question: P and Q can complete a work in 9 days and 15 days, respectively. If they work together for three days, then in how many days will the remaining work be completed by Q alone?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q can complete a work in 9 days and 15 days, respectively. If they work together for three days, then in how many days will the remaining work be completed by Q alone?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken to complete a work by P = 9 days

Time taken to complete a work by Q = 15 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

LCM of 9 and 15 is 45

Efficiency of P = (45/9) = 5 units/day

Efficiency of Q = (45/15) = 3 units/day

P and Q worked together for 3 days = [3 × (5 + 3)]

⇒ (3 × 8) = 24 units

Remaining work = (45 – 24) = 21 units

Now,

The remaining work completed by Q alone = (21/3)

⇒ 7 days

∴ The required days is 7

questions.question: 16 persons working 6 hours a day can complete a work in 10 days. In how many days 24 persons working 8 hours a day will complete 80% of that work?
questions.questionHtml: 16 persons working 6 hours a day can complete a work in 10 days. In how many days 24 persons working 8 hours a day will complete 80% of that work?
questions.solution:
As we know, Total work = Total work, so

M1 × T1 × D­1 = M2 × T2 × D2

Given, M1 = 16 person, T1 = 6 hrs, D1 = 10 days, Let W1 = 100%, M2 = 24 person, T2 = 8 hrs, W2 = 80% and D2 = ?

(M1 × D1 × T1)/W1 = (M2 × T2 × D2)/W2

(16 × 10 × 6)/100% = (24 × 8 × D2)/80%

D2 = 4 days.

questions.question: A can do a work in 30 days, B can do the same work in 48 days. After working alone for 20 days A left and B started working, how long will B take to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a work in 30 days, B can do the same work in 48 days. After working alone for 20 days A left and B started working, how long will B take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
Detailed Solution∶

Efficiency of A = 1/30

Efficiency of B = 1/48

Work done by A in 20 days = 20/30 = 2/3

Remaining work = 1 – (2/3) = 1/3

Number of days taken by B to complete the work = (1/3) / (1/48) = 16 days

Alternate Solution∶

Work done by A in 2 days = 20 × 8 = 160

Remaining work = 240 – 160 = 80

Number of days taken by B = 80/5 = 16 days

questions.question: The efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 2 ∶ 5 ∶ 7 working together, they can complete a work in 10 days. In how many days will, A alone be able to complete 30% of that work?
questions.questionHtml: The efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 2 ∶ 5 ∶ 7 working together, they can complete a work in 10 days. In how many days will, A alone be able to complete 30% of that work?

⇒ Total work = 10 × (2M + 5M + 7M) = 140M

A alone can complete the work in = 140M/2M = 70 days

To complete 30% of work, A will take = 70 × 30/100 = 21 days

questions.question: If Mona and Sona together can finish a typing work in 18 days and Sona alone can finish it in 24 days, find the number of days in which Mona alone can finish the work.
questions.questionHtml: If Mona and Sona together can finish a typing work in 18 days and Sona alone can finish it in 24 days, find the number of days in which Mona alone can finish the work.
questions.solution:
( mona + sona )'s efficiency =  total work /no. of  days = 72 ÷ 18 = 4      ----(1)

 sona  alone finishes 72 unit work in 24 days

efficiency of sona = total work ÷ no.of days = 72 ÷ 24 = 3      ----(2)

Now, on subtracting eq.(1) from eq (2), we get 

mona efficiency = ( mona + sona )'s efficiency - sona efficiency  = (4 -3) =1 

No. of days in which mona alone finishes work  = total work ÷ mona's efficiency  ⇒ ( 72 ÷ 1 ) = 72 days .

= 1/9 + 1/12 + 1/18 = (4 + 3 + 2)/36 = 9/36 = 1/4 (work/day)

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 hours and 4 hours, respectively, while a third pipe can empty it in 12 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty tank if all the three pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes can fill a tank in 15 hours and 4 hours, respectively, while a third pipe can empty it in 12 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty tank if all the three pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time to fill the tank by two pipes = 15 hours and 4 hours

Time to empty the tank by third pipe = 12 hours

Concept used:

If Pipe A take ‘x’ hours and Pipe B takes ‘y’ hours to fill a tank then assume the total capacity of the tank is equal to LCM of ‘x’ and ‘y’ or a multiple of them.

Formula used:

Efficiency = Total work/total time

Calculations:

Let the total capacity of the tank be LCM of 15, 4, and 12 i.e. 60 units.

The efficiency of the first pipe = 60/15

⇒ 4 units/hour

The efficiency of the second pipe = 60/4

⇒ 15 units/hour

The efficiency of the third pipe = 60/12

⇒ 5 units/hour

Combined efficiency of three pipes = 4 + 15 - 5

⇒ 14 units/hour

Time to empty the tank by all the pipes together = 60/14

⇒ 30/7 hours

∴ It takes 30/7 hours to fill the empty tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously.

Shortcut Trick Total work = 60 unit

          A          B           C
Efficiency         4         15           -5

 

Total efficiency = 4 + 15 - 5 = 14

∴ Time is taken to fill the tank = 60/14 = 30/7 hours

questions.question: A can complete a certain work in 35 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They worked together for 7 days, then B left the work. In how many days will A alone complete 60% of the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a certain work in 35 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. They worked together for 7 days, then B left the work. In how many days will A alone complete 60% of the remaining work?
questions.solution:
GIven:

A completes the work in 35 days

B completes the work in 15 days

Concept used:

A's one day work is 1/35

B's one day work is 1/15

Calculation:

A + B = (1/35) + (1/15)

⇒ A + B = (7 + 3)/105 = 2/21

Work completed by A + B in 7 days 

⇒ (2/21) × 7 = 2/3

Remaining work = 1 - (2/3) = 1/3

1/3 work is left 

A will complete it in = 35 × (1/3) = 35/3

Asked in question 60% of the remaining work

⇒ (35/3) × (60/100) =7

∴ A will take 7 days.

By LCM method

              Time      Total work(LCM of time)  Efficiency(total work/time)

A             35                                                         3

                                        105

B             15                                                         7 

A + B = 3 + 7 =10

A + B workes for 7 days = 10 × 7 = 70

Reamning work = 105 - 70 = 35

60% of the remaining work = 35 × (60/100) = 21

A complete it = 21/3 = 7

∴ A will take 7 days.

questions.question: If 27 people, working 8 hours a day, can complete a task in 12 days, then in how many days will 18 people finish the task, working 9 hours a day?
questions.questionHtml: If 27 people, working 8 hours a day, can complete a task in 12 days, then in how many days will 18 people finish the task, working 9 hours a day?
questions.solution:
Calculations:

⇒ Let the number of days required to complete the task by 18 people, working 9 hours per day is 'd'.

(M1 × D1 × H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W2

⇒ (M1 × D1 × H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W2

⇒ (27 × 12 × 8)/1 = (18 × d × 9)/1

⇒ d = 16

∴ The number of days required to complete the task by 18 people, working 9 hours per day is '16'.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 9 days and B in 12 days. If they work together on it for 5 days, then the fraction of the work left is:

questions.question: 14 men complete a work in 10 days. If 7 men are employed, then in how many days will they complete the same work?

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 16 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, starting with pipe A first. In how many hours, the empty tank will be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 16 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, starting with pipe A first. In how many hours, the empty tank will be filled?
questions.solution:
Pipe A's 1 hour's work = 1/10

Pipe B's 1 hour's work = 1/16

Pipe (A + B)’s 2 hours work = 1/10 + 1/16 = 13/80

Pipe (A + B)’ 12 hours work = 6 × 13/80 = 78/80 = 39/40

Remaining fraction of work after 12 hours = 1 – 39/40 = 1/40

This work will be done by A in = 1/40 × 10 = 1/4 hours

Total time = 12 + 1/4 = 49/4 hours = \(12\frac{1}{4}{\rm{hours}}\)

questions.question: Rakshit, Ajay, and Satish are sanitation workers in a Municipal Corporation. In how many hours, can Satish complete the work alone?
questions.questionHtml: Rakshit, Ajay, and Satish are sanitation workers in a Municipal Corporation. Rakshit alone takes 20 hours to clean a drain while Ajay takes 12 hours when working alone to do the same. All three together take only 5 hours to clean the drain. questions.solution:
Alternate Method Suppose total work is 60 units (LCM of 5, 12 and 20)

Efficiency of all three = 60 / 5 = 12

Efficiency of Rakshit = 60 / 20 = 3

Efficiency of Ajay = 60 / 12 = 5

Efficiency of Satish = (12 - 8) = 4

Number of days taken by Satish alone to finish the work = 60 / 4 = 15 days

questions.question: A can do a certain work in 15 days, while B can do the same work in 21 days. If they work together, then in how many days will the same work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a certain work in 15 days, while B can do the same work in 21 days. If they work together, then in how many days will the same work be completed?
questions.solution:
Work done by A in 1 day = \(1\over 15\),  Work done by B in 1 day = \(1\over 21\)

Total work done by A and B in 1 day = \(1\over 15\) + \(1\over 21\) = \(36\over 21\times 15\)

TIme taken to complete total work = \(21\times 15\over 36\) = 8\(3\over 4\) days.

questions.question: Akhil can complete a piece of work in 24 days. Shyam can complete the same piece of work in 12 days. If both of them work together, in how many days can they complete the same piece of work?
questions.questionHtml: Akhil can complete a piece of work in 24 days. Shyam can complete the same piece of work in 12 days. If both of them work together, in how many days can they complete the same piece of work?
questions.solution:
Work rate of Akhil = 1/24 work/day, Work rate of Shyam = 1/12 work/day

Total work rate when working together = 1/24 + 2/24 = 3/24 = 1/8

Time taken to complete the work together = 1 / (1/8) = 8 days

questions.question: A can do \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the work in 3 days and B can do \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the work in 7.5 days . Working together, A and B can do \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the same work in:
questions.questionHtml: A can do \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the work in 3 days and B can do \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the work in 7.5 days . Working together, A and B can do \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the same work in:
questions.solution:
Time taken by A to complete the work = \(\frac{1}{5}\times\frac{1}{3}\) = \(\frac{1}{15}\)

Time taken by B to complete the work = \(\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{1}{7.5}\) = \(\frac{1}{30}\)

Time taken to complete the whole work together = \(\frac{1}{15}+\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{10}\) = 10 days

According to the question,

Time taken to complete \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the work together = \(\frac{4}{5}\times10=8\) days.

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 10 and 16 days respectively. A begins to do the work and they work alternatively one at a time for one day each. The whole work will be completed in:
questions.questionHtml: A and B can complete a piece of work in 10 and 16 days respectively. A begins to do the work and they work alternatively one at a time for one day each. The whole work will be completed in:
questions.solution:
Let the total work be 80 units

In 12 days work completed = 78 units

Now,The remaining 2 units will be completed by A in 2/8 days or 1/4 days

questions.question: The efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 4 ∶ 5 ∶ 6. Working together, they can complete a work in 12 days. In how many days will A alone be able to complete that work?
questions.questionHtml: The efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 4 ∶ 5 ∶ 6. Working together, they can complete a work in 12 days. In how many days will A alone be able to complete that work?
questions.solution:
Total work = sum of efficiencies × time taken together

Total work = (4 + 5 + 6) × 12 = 180 units

A alone will take = total work/A’s individual efficiency

⇒ 180/4 = 45 days

questions.question: Tom can do a piece of work in 7 days, whereas Jay can do the same work in 14 days. How long will they take to finish the work if both work together?
questions.questionHtml: Tom can do a piece of work in 7 days, whereas Jay can do the same work in 14 days. How long will they take to finish the work if both work together?
questions.solution:
⇒ Tom's rate = 1/7 of the work per day  ⇒ Jay's rate = 1/14 of the work per day

⇒ 1/7 + 1/14 = 2/14 + 1/14 = 3/14 of the work per day

Time taken when working together ⇒ 1 / (3/14) = 14/3 days or \(4 \frac{2}{3}\rm days\).

questions.question: P can work thrice as fast as Q. Working independently, Q can complete a task in 24 days. In how many days can P and Q together finish the same task?
questions.questionHtml: P can work thrice as fast as Q. Working independently, Q can complete a task in 24 days. In how many days can P and Q together finish the same task?
questions.solution:
Given:

Efficiency of P = 3 × Efficiency of Q

Q can complete the work in 24 days

Formula used:

Total work = efficiency × Time period

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of P be 3x

Let the efficiency of Q be x

Total work = 24 × x

P and Q can complete the (24 × x) work in {(24 × x)/(3x + x)} days

⇒ 24/4 = 6

∴ P and Q together finish the same task in 6 days.

questions.question: It takes A and B, 3 and 6 hours, respectively, to complete a certain work. If they work on the alternate hour. How long will it take them to accomplish the task?
questions.questionHtml: It takes A and B, 3 and 6 hours, respectively, to complete a certain work. If they work on the alternate hour. How long will it take them to accomplish the task?
questions.solution:
Given : 

A can do work in 3 hours.

B can do work in 6 hours.

Formula Used : 

Work done = time × efficiency

Calculation : 

Total work = LCM(3, 6) = 6 

Efficiency of A = 2

Efficiency of B = 1

Since they work on alternate days starting with A,

So,

⇒ 2 hours = 3 units 

Now to complete 6 units of work 

⇒ 2 × 2 hours = 3 × 2 units

⇒ 4 hours = 6 units

∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.

questions.question: Anjali is designing a wall for a social purpose. She completed \(7 \over 11\) work in 14 days. In how many days will she complete the rest of the work?
questions.questionHtml: Anjali is designing a wall for a social purpose. She completed \(7 \over 11\) work in 14 days. In how many days will she complete the rest of the work?

14 days for 7/11 work.

For 1/11 work, she took 14/7 = 2 days

So, for 4/11 she will need 4x2 = 8 days

questions.question: A is twice as good a workman as B, and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days. In how many days will A alone finish the work ?
questions.questionHtml: A is twice as good a workman as B, and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days. In how many days will A alone finish the work ?
questions.solution:
Given:

The efficiency of A = 2 × Efficiency of B 

Total time is taken to do work together = 13 days

Concept used:

Time = 1/Efficiency

Calculation:

Let the time taken by A to complete work alone be x days. 

The time is taken by B to complete work alone is x days. 

1 day work of A = 1/x

1 day work of B = 1/2x

1 day work of A and B together = 1/13

⇒ 1 day work of A + B = 1/x + 1/2x

⇒ 1/13 = (2 + 1)/2x

⇒ 2x = 39

⇒ x = 39/2 days

⇒ x = \(19 \frac{1}{2}\) days

∴ The time taken by A alone to finish the work is \(19 \frac{1}{2}\) days.

Shortcut Trick

  Efficiency The efficiency of (A + B)
   A 2 3
  B 1

 

Total Work = 3 × 13 = 39

Total time is taken by A = Total work/Efficiency of A

⇒ 39/2 = 19\(\frac{1}{2}\)

∴ The time taken by A alone to finish the work is 19\(\frac{1}{2}\)  days

questions.question: X and Y together finish a task in 12 days. If Y alone can finish the same task in 15 days, then how many days will X alone take to finish the task?
questions.questionHtml: X and Y together finish a task in 12 days. If Y alone can finish the same task in 15 days, then how many days will X alone take to finish the task?
questions.solution:
Given:          

X and Y together finish a task in 12 day.

Y alone can finish the same task in 15 days.

Formula used:

Total work = Efficiency × Time Taken

Calculation:

X and Y together finish a task in 12 days.

In day X and Y can done the work = 1/12 part of the work

Y alone can finish the same task in 15 days.

In one day Y can done the work = 1/15 part of the work

In 1 day X can does of the work = (1/12) – (1/15)

⇒ (5 – 4)/60

⇒ 1/60

So, X can does of the work in 60 days.

∴ X can does of the work in 60 days.
